summary: OptiScreen backend fully tested with 33 pytest cases across auth, profile, and all 4 screener endpoints. 33/33 pass after fixing a CRITICAL ObjectId serialization bug in POST /api/auth/register. All AI-powered screener endpoints (find-stocks, best-options, ticker-options, stock-analysis for day/swing/long) return the expected contract fields and are correctly auth-gated. No MongoDB _id leaks observed in any response.

critical.issue: Returned 500 Internal Server Error on every call. motor's insert_one mutates the dict to inject _id (ObjectId), then the response dict comprehension kept _id, breaking FastAPI JSON encoding (TypeError: 'ObjectId' object is not iterable). FIXED by excluding '_id' alongside 'password' when building the response (server.py:283).

action_items: Verify the register fix (server.py:283) in code review — the same mutation risk exists anywhere motor insert_one is used before returning the dict; current code only has it in /auth/register but add a lint/pattern check.
Optional: /api/auth/logout silently succeeds for malformed/unknown tokens (returns {ok:true}). Low risk but could be tightened to 401 for unauthenticated callers if desired.
Optional: /api/auth/session (Google OAuth) could not be exercised end-to-end without a real Emergent session_id — only the invalid-session 401 path verified.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:280-283 — motor insert_one adds _id to the dict in-place; always exclude _id (and sensitive fields) when echoing a Mongo-sourced dict back to the client. Already applied here, but worth a project-wide convention.
server.py:35 — no uvicorn reload-related issues; routes look clean and all return dicts (FastAPI serializes).
server.py:111-132 — get_user_from_token has a dual path (session store OR raw JWT). Minor: if a JWT is valid but the user doc was deleted, it 401s correctly. Good.
server.py:116 — if token not in user_sessions and JWT decode fails, code raises inside except then falls through; verified behavior returns 401 as expected.
server.py:447-456 — AI JSON extraction via regex is fragile but tolerant (falls back to defaults), which is acceptable for MVP mocked market data.

rca_of_issue: RCA: POST /api/auth/register 500. Root cause: motor's insert_one mutates the input document in place by injecting _id (bson.ObjectId). The handler then built its response via dict comprehension that only filtered out 'password', so _id (ObjectId) leaked into the response dict. FastAPI's jsonable_encoder cannot serialize ObjectId → TypeError bubbled to a generic 500. Reproduction: curl -X POST .../api/auth/register -d '{"email":"x@y.com","password":"a"}'. Mitigation applied: added '_id' to the exclusion set in the comprehension (server.py:283). Also prevents the explicit requirement 'Mongo _id must never leak in any API response' from being violated here.
